author: Maya
text: Let's use this thread for the final product rehearsal. We need a realistic conversation that shows upload, filtering, graph expansion, fullscreen, and summaries.

author: Owen
text: I can start with the problem statement: long discussion threads are hard to scan when everything is linear.

author: Priya
text: Then we can upload the JSON and show that the dataset selector updates without leaving the page.

author: Caleb
text: The live upload is a strong moment. It proves the app is not only displaying hardcoded demo data.

author: Zoe
text: Let's make sure the uploaded file has a few different topics so the chips are useful right away.

author: Nikhil
text: I would also include some balanced sentiment labels. A totally positive thread makes the footer less interesting.

author: Sofia
text: Agreed. We can include a few concerns about timing, graph density, and network reliability.

author: Eli
text: Those concerns are realistic and still keep the thread collaborative.

author: Harper
text: For the graph section, I want to show the roots first, then expand all nodes to reveal the conversation structure.

author: Maya
text: Good. After that, collapse all nodes and open only one branch so people can see how exploration works.

author: Owen
text: Fullscreen should come after we expand the graph. It will make the layout easier to see from the back of the room.

author: Priya
text: And we should mention that fullscreen keeps the topic and time controls available.

author: Caleb
text: That is useful because we can filter while still keeping the graph large.

author: Zoe
text: The fullscreen button should not reset which nodes are open. That would be confusing during a live demo.

author: Nikhil
text: Right, it should feel like resizing the same view, not starting over.

author: Sofia
text: I checked that behavior after the latest change. Expanded branches stay open when entering fullscreen.

author: Eli
text: Great. That will make the graph demo feel much smoother.

author: Harper
text: Can we make the time filter part of the demo? It shows that the app is more than just a static diagram.

author: Maya
text: Yes. We can narrow the range to one or two days and show the graph update.

author: Owen
text: The topic chips should also change when the selected time range changes.

author: Priya
text: That is a nice detail, but we should not linger too long unless someone asks.

author: Caleb
text: Agreed. The main story is still upload, map, filter, summary.

author: Zoe
text: The time filter is useful as a quick proof that the graph is dynamic.

author: Nikhil
text: Let's use week view during the demo because the labels are easier to read.

author: Sofia
text: I want to make sure the chat view still has a place in the walkthrough.

author: Eli
text: Maybe use chat view after selecting a topic. It lets people read the actual conversation behind the graph.

author: Harper
text: The reply preview in chat view is helpful. It shows context without opening every message.

author: Maya
text: We should open one message detail sheet from the map and one from chat view if time allows.

author: Owen
text: That might be too much for the main demo, but it is good backup material for questions.

author: Priya
text: Let's keep it in the script as optional, then decide based on time.

author: Caleb
text: I ran the longer upload file locally. The dataset loaded and the message count matched.

author: Zoe
text: Did the graph stay responsive after expanding all branches?

author: Caleb
text: Yes. It was dense, but the fit-to-view behavior made it manageable.

author: Nikhil
text: We should avoid expanding everything on the phone. The screen is too small for that to be useful.

author: Sofia
text: True. On phone, it is better to use topic filters and open one branch at a time.

author: Eli
text: For the actual showcase, the projector should be the main view. The phone is more of a quick compatibility check.

author: Harper
text: The backend also needs to be warmed up before we test from another device.

author: Maya
text: Let's load the selected dataset once on the laptop before connecting the phone.

author: Owen
text: I will also check the API route directly from the phone browser if the page looks empty.

author: Priya
text: Good plan. If the API route returns datasets, then the frontend path is fine.

author: Caleb
text: What should we say about AI summaries if the API key is not available during the showcase?

author: Zoe
text: We can say the app uses cached or fallback summaries when live AI is not configured.

author: Nikhil
text: The important part is that summary cards are tied to thread roots.

author: Sofia
text: Exactly. They help explain what each branch is about before expanding it.

author: Eli
text: One limitation is that summaries can take time to generate on first load.

author: Harper
text: We can frame that as a normal tradeoff for AI-enriched analysis.

author: Maya
text: Let's pre-load the dataset so the showcase focuses on the user experience, not waiting.

author: Owen
text: I can handle that setup before we present.

author: Priya
text: Let's rehearse with the long file once so we know where the most interesting branches are.

author: Caleb
text: I suggest using the fullscreen branch because it shows a concern and then the fix.

author: Zoe
text: The mobile testing branch is also useful if someone asks about joining from a phone.

author: Nikhil
text: Maybe keep that as a backup answer instead of part of the main demo.

author: Sofia
text: Good idea. The main path should be polished and short.

author: Eli
text: We can mention the rest during questions if people want more detail.

author: Harper
text: I will mark the branches we want to open during rehearsal.

author: Maya
text: Let's time the full walkthrough after lunch.

author: Owen
text: I can keep notes on any points where the demo feels slow.

author: Priya
text: Perfect. If a section drags, we can trim the narration rather than remove the feature.

author: Caleb
text: I want to confirm the data model we are showing: id, author, timestamp, text, parentId, topic, and sentiment.

author: Zoe
text: That is enough for the frontend to build threads and show filters immediately.

author: Nikhil
text: We should not add unusual cases to this showcase file. It is meant to demonstrate the happy path.

author: Sofia
text: Right. Save validation edge cases for testing, not presentation.

author: Eli
text: The parent ids should form a few deep branches and a few broad branches.

author: Harper
text: That makes the map look more realistic than a single straight chain.

author: Maya
text: The longer file should feel like a real team conversation, not generated filler.

author: Owen
text: We can vary authors and keep the message tone natural.

author: Priya
text: One practical concern: the longer upload may take a little longer to summarize.

author: Caleb
text: That is fine if we warm it up before the showcase.

author: Zoe
text: If it feels slow, we can use the shorter file for live upload and the longer file for graph exploration.

author: Nikhil
text: That is a smart fallback. The short file proves upload, and the long file proves scale.

author: Sofia
text: We should keep both files available in the project root so they are easy to find.

author: Eli
text: I will name them clearly so we do not pick the wrong one while presenting.

author: Harper
text: The long file should also have enough roots to make the collapse state meaningful.

author: Maya
text: Yes, multiple roots make the overview mode useful.

author: Owen
text: Let's assign final responsibilities so everyone knows what they are presenting.

author: Priya
text: I will handle upload and explain the expected JSON shape.

author: Caleb
text: I can present the map controls, including expand all and fullscreen.

author: Zoe
text: I will explain topic filtering and how it changes the visible conversation.

author: Nikhil
text: I can cover sentiment and the footer summary.

author: Sofia
text: I will close with limitations and next steps.

author: Eli
text: I'll keep an eye on time and signal if we need to skip optional parts.

author: Harper
text: I will run the backend and watch the terminal during the demo.

author: Maya
text: Great. That splits the work evenly.

author: Owen
text: One last thing: let's keep the file names visible in Finder so upload is quick.

author: Priya
text: I did a full run with the short file. The upload step took only a few seconds.

author: Caleb
text: The long file is better for showing the map, though. It has more structure.

author: Zoe
text: Maybe start with short upload, then select the long dataset if we want a richer map.

author: Nikhil
text: That is a bit of a switch, but it could work if we explain it clearly.

author: Sofia
text: I would rather upload the long file once and use it for the whole walkthrough.

author: Eli
text: I agree with Sofia. One dataset keeps the story simpler.

author: Harper
text: Then the shorter file can be our backup if we need a faster upload.

author: Maya
text: Let's do that. Long file for the main showcase, short file as backup.

author: Owen
text: I will rehearse the opening with the long dataset selected.

author: Priya
text: I will make sure the upload file is available locally before class.

author: Caleb
text: Final technical checklist: backend running, frontend running, dataset warmed, browser opened, projector mirrored.

author: Zoe
text: Also confirm the phone can reach the frontend IP if we want to mention cross-device access.

author: Nikhil
text: If phone data does not load, check the API route directly before debugging the UI.

author: Sofia
text: Good note. The app page can load while the backend data route still fails.

author: Eli
text: I will keep the laptop on the same Wi-Fi as the phone to avoid network surprises.

author: Harper
text: The rest of the checklist looks good.

author: Maya
text: Let's do one last pass on the actual demo sequence.

author: Owen
text: Sequence: upload JSON, select dataset, expand map, fullscreen map, filter by topic, show footer summary, return to chat view.

author: Priya
text: That sequence feels complete and not too complicated.

author: Caleb
text: We should stop after the chat view unless there are questions.

author: Zoe
text: Agreed. Ending with the chat view connects the graph back to the original messages.

author: Nikhil
text: This should be enough to show both the technical work and the user value.

author: Sofia
text: I feel good about it. The flow is much clearer than it was last week.

author: Eli
text: Same. Let's freeze the demo files and avoid last-minute changes unless something breaks.

author: Harper
text: I will keep copies of all three showcase files in the root folder.

author: Maya
text: Perfect. We are ready for the showcase.
